title: Galdr Hardanger fiddle augmentation validation results
summary: Completed epoch-150 results from the prespecified original-versus-conventional checkpoint campaign, plus fixed-checkpoint leave-one-family-out, targeted successor, preference, recipe, and late-training interaction experiments with the compact Galdr AMT model.

guidance: Use these results to form hypotheses for a corpus with similar recording and instrument characteristics.
Choose transform strengths and exposure schedules for the target corpus and validate them on untouched held-out source groups.
Do not treat the best Galdr arm as an AMT-Augmentor package default.

protocols.question: Does the conventional six-view augmentation package improve the compact model over original-only training at the same fixed training horizon?
protocols.design: Both arms use seed 424242, 150 epochs, 36000 optimizer updates, the same source-disjoint split, and the same evaluation. The update budget is matched; O repeatedly samples originals while C samples one original and five transformed logical views. The campaign evaluated 30 prespecified candidates at five-epoch intervals; the observations in this card are the fixed epoch-150 rows, not winner-selected scores.

winner_rule: exact tie: highest full-precision tune-macro onset-only F1

protocols.question: Which pitch, reverb, or time-variation treatment is most promising when total source/window/logical-slot exposure is held fixed?
protocols.design: Every arm has 72 logical slots and 2880000 total draws. The p1 control has 48 original, 12 archival-noise, and 12 legacy-pitch slots. Pitch arms replace the 12 pitch slots. RF, reverb, and time arms replace 12 of p1's 48 original slots, leaving 36 original, 12 archival-noise, 12 legacy-pitch, and 12 treatment slots. This controls the number of changed logical slots, total draws, and optimizer steps; pitch-grid substitution and adding a new family still answer different questions.

derived_results.interpretation: The conventional package improved both validation metrics at the fixed epoch-150 horizon.
Removing gain/chorus improved both metrics inside the dense package.
Removing generic Gaussian noise traded lower onset F1 for slightly higher onset-plus-offset F1.
Removing the combined reverb/filter family improved both metrics inside the dense package.
Pitch shift was the only conventional family whose removal clearly hurt both metrics.
Removing global stretch was almost neutral for onsets and improved onset-plus-offset F1 inside the dense package.
Archival noise/hum improved both metrics over its slot-matched duplicated-original control.
Fractional detuning was mixed against its slot-matched control.
The compact four-shift grid improved both metrics over legacy pitch.
The wide four-shift grid gave only a small improvement.
The dense twelve-shift grid improved both metrics over legacy pitch, but did not dominate p4 on onset-plus-offset F1.
Combined reverb/filter exposure improved both metrics in the simplified preference context.
Moderate reverb did not improve the p1 control.
Strong reverb improved both metrics and outperformed moderate reverb.
Global stretch was the strongest preference-screen treatment on both metrics.
Local time warp improved both metrics but did not match global stretch.
Adding detuning hurt both metrics at epoch 100.
Adding detuning hurt both metrics at epoch 150.
Late RF exposure alone was mixed.
Late global-stretch exposure alone was slightly positive.
The two late exposures together improved both metrics more than either exposure alone.
The descriptive interaction was positive, especially for onset-plus-offset F1; that interaction was positive on all six tunes for the primary metric.

interpretations: Augmentation as a whole improved the fixed-horizon compact Galdr validation result over original-only training.
Pitch shifting is the clearest retained conventional family: removing it from the dense package hurt both metrics, and targeted pitch grids improved on the legacy-pitch control.
Corpus-matched archival noise/hum improved both metrics over its slot-matched control and is more informative for this archive domain than assuming generic Gaussian noise is sufficient.
Global time stretch was the strongest treatment in the controlled preference screen; local time warp helped but was weaker.

Reverb results are strength- and context-dependent. Moderate reverb was neutral to negative, strong reverb was positive, and the combined RF family changed sign between the dense leave-one-out context and the simplified preference context.
Fractional detuning should not be added to the archival-plus-pitch recipe on this evidence: the exact APD-minus-AP comparison was negative at both checkpoints.

A targeted Galdr mixture is justified as a dataset-specific engineering choice because it avoids settings with negative or redundant conditional evidence and makes exposure explicit; these experiments do not identify a universally optimal number of families or clean-to-augmented fraction.
limitations: Every model result uses one initialization and data-order seed, 424242.
All reported model comparisons use six validation tunes; there are no test-set claims and no multi-seed uncertainty estimates.
The studies support engineering decisions for the current hf2-group-v2 corpus, not universal rankings of AMT augmentation methods.
LOFO effects are conditional on the dense conventional package and can change when competing families or their exposure frequencies change.

The preference design changes 12 logical slots in every treatment arm, but pitch arms substitute one pitch grid for another while reverb and time arms replace original slots; those contrasts answer different questions even though their exposure counts match.
RF denotes a combined reverb plus high/low-pass filtering treatment, so its results do not isolate reverb from filtering.
The RF by global-stretch interaction is post-hoc, begins after a shared epoch-100 checkpoint, applies treatments on separate draws, and is descriptive rather than a full-course factorial estimate.

The O/C campaign had a prespecified 30-candidate validation grid and winner rule. The O/C values in this card are fixed epoch-150 rows and must not be described as the campaign's winner-selected estimates.

The Galdr experiments span evolving AMT-Augmentor and Galdr source trees. The local Galdr control revision binds the protocol configs, but no single historical AMT-Augmentor revision is claimed across all results.
The exact Galdr control revision and its protocol configs must be published or bundled before external release; they are currently recorded as unpublished.
Canonical evaluation artifacts are identified by locator and SHA-256 but are not redistributed in this package.
